assessment.status_reason: The central premise that the existing silica fiber can be reused for MIR ATR is contradicted by the sources: silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR light, which requires CIR or PIR fibers or hollow waveguides. Approval of the concept as stated is therefore not possible; the MIR ATR method itself remains worth testing with the correct fiber.

solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level data fusion combines synchronized MIR ATR and NIR spectra into a single augmented matrix with autoscaling. Both probes must sample the exact same process volume simultaneously to avoid turbulence-induced discrepancies. The multi-block model must demonstrate superior prediction accuracy over the best single method on independent validation batches before deployment.

assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The target is continuous in-line tracking of water content; once calibrated, the fiber-probe setup supports near-real-time results, subject to the confirmed link and acquisition conditions.
assessment.future_direction: If the process later needs more than water (e.g. composition fingerprinting), a multispectral extension building on the same probe infrastructure could be considered.

assessment.status_reason: The central premise that the existing silica fiber can be reused for MIR ATR is contradicted by the sources: silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR light, which requires CIR or PIR fibers or hollow waveguides. Approval of the concept as stated is therefore not possible; the MIR ATR method itself remains worth testing with the correct fiber.

premise_checks.premise: The existing silica fiber cable from a visible/NIR setup can be reused for MIR ATR.
premise_checks.explanation: Silica fibers end near 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR light; MIR requires chalcogenide (CIR), polycrystalline (PIR) fibers or hollow waveguides.

solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level data fusion combines synchronized MIR ATR and NIR spectra into a single augmented matrix with autoscaling. Both probes must sample the exact same process volume simultaneously to avoid turbulence-induced discrepancies. The multi-block model must demonstrate superior prediction accuracy over the best single method on independent validation batches before deployment.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A quantitative water-in-petroleum model (e.g. PLS on MIR ATR spectra) will need representative calibration samples and independent reference values; validation on held-out samples is essential before any in-line use.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The target is continuous in-line tracking of water content; once calibrated, the fiber-probe setup supports near-real-time results, subject to the confirmed link and acquisition conditions.
assessment.future_direction: If the process later needs more than water (e.g. composition fingerprinting), a multispectral extension building on the same probe infrastructure could be considered.

proposal.what_would_change_it: A confirmed MIR fiber link length and sample state would fix the installation; if the MIR link proves infeasible, the NIR fallback over the existing silica cable becomes the primary path.
proposal.next_step: Supply the link length, routing and operating conditions, and run the laboratory MIR ATR feasibility test on representative petroleum samples with Karl Fischer reference values.

assessment.brief_answer: The concept cannot be approved as stated: silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR light, so MIR ATR needs a CIR or PIR fiber instead of the existing cable. MIR ATR itself is worth testing first, with a published precedent for water in petroleum. Open items: the MIR link length to the other building, the sample state, and the required accuracy.
